While the direction and amount differ, the specific subject matter (the commercial allowance for loan and lease losses) is identical. The matching agent grouped this, and it is a valid one-to-one alignment of the same financial metric.

The 2024 disclosure D277 contains specific narrative metrics on total commercial utilized credit exposure ($739.5 billion) and the aggregate utilization rate (55%). The 2025 disclosure D276 contains the corresponding narrative metrics for 2025 (exposure $808.4 billion, utilization rate 55%). D277 in 2025 only contains structural references to tables and lacks the exposure narrative, making D276 the valid counterpart for the specific topic covered in 2024 D277.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, loans increased by $19.8 billion due to higher loans in CIB and securities-based lending in AWM, while lending-related commitments decreased by $5.3 billion due to decreases in AWM and CCB, largely offset by higher commitments in CIB.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclosed specific increases in their commercial or corporate loan portfolios during 2024. BAC reported a $43.2 billion increase in total commercial utilized credit exposure driven by higher loans and leases. Similarly, JPM reported that loans increased by $19.8 billion, driven by higher loans in the Corporate and Investment Bank (CIB). Both disclosures highlight growth in funded loan balances as a key driver of credit exposure volume.

As of December 31, 2024, loans increased $19.8 billion, driven by higher loans in CIB and higher securities-based lending in AWM.
